THE SHAPE (neutral reproducer, run on the tree, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    my @w = map split, "a b", " c  d ";
    print scalar(@w), " @w\n";

    perl: 4 a b c d
    PCL : Unhandled sb-int:simple-program-error ... invalid number of arguments: 1   + a Lisp backtrace (exit 1)

    Controls that work: `my @w = split;` with $_ set, and `map { split } "p q"`.

WHERE (emitted Lisp): `(p-map (lambda ($_) (p-split $_)) "a b" " c  d ")` -- the EXPR-form path supplies the default operand
as the FIRST argument (the pattern slot) and no string; the block-form path builds the full default `split ' ', $_`.  Two
lowerings of the zero-argument builtin (rule 11: one place should own the defaults of `split`).
UNTIDY half: a wrong-arity call to a runtime function is an internal error that reaches the user raw (#1427's census).

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (taken): 1359 with `map { split } <DATA>` is byte-identical to perl -- its only cause.

FIX (Pl/PExpr.pm): `add_implicit_default_param` is the ONE owner of split's defaults (a bare `split` is `split ' ', $_`,
`split /PAT/` is `split /PAT/, $_`); the two copies in handle_subcalls' argument-list paths are deleted.  The
zero-argument path (a -2 builtin followed by a binary-only operator: `map split, LIST`, `grep split, LIST`,
`(split, 1)`) asked only the generic rule and emitted `(p-split $_)`.  `CORE::split /,/` gets its $_ now too.
